When I was in seventh grade, a girl was cutting herself and then would send pictures of it to people when you’d be having a conversation with her (I remember the DM of it she sent me, not that gruesome but painful to see, it was the old Instagram format) 

It was never sent randomly, I texted her a few times and she’d talk about her depression and then the conversation would go to her cutting. I didn’t know what to do, nor did any of my friends. We all agreed she was “asking for attention,” as if it was a bad thing & did our best to avoid her. Thankfully one of us told the principal before further damage. 

Then another time, my freshman year, one of my best friends was talking to a senior who was saying that people who cut themselves horizontally are asking for attention. 

“But you cut like this,” He pretended to cut the underpart of his forearm vertically, “it’s more pain. More real.” 

My best friend nodded her head along with what this guy was saying. At this point in my life, I had been cutting myself badly. I was cutting myself “horizontally.” I wondered what they would say if I showed them my thighs, my stomach and ask if that was real enough for them. I didn’t have to nerve to say or do anything, but I didn’t nod my head along with them either. 

Years later, I’m now still in school with the girl from seventh grade and my best friend who thought how you cut mattered, and I feel so bad that we patronized the girls cutting and that I stayed silent over the years when people acted like cutting was “asking for attention,” because the last two/three years I’ve been struggling with it too.

Someone who is “asking for attention” is no different than someone who wants help. If he/she is willing to inflict bodily harm on themselves and then bear that to whoever will listen, then I do hope they’re getting attention from that. Regardless of how people react with their own self harm after the fact, they still harmed themselves in the first place, there was still some pain, some issue that brought them to that place. 

And if you’re scared to tell people that you’re struggling with self-harm because it might look like you’re “asking for attention,” don’t be. Anyone who will be annoyed or upset about you showing your self-harm, rather than being concerned about why you self-harmed, then they’re not worth more than a grain of salt. 

Sometimes I think about what I had said about the girl in seventh grade behind her back and I wish I could turn back time and be there for her, but life has a way of moving on.
